questions.q: What happens when CNOT (control=q2, target=q1) is applied to the Bell state (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2?
options: It destroys all superposition, giving a single basis state
It converts the state into (|01⟩+|10⟩)/√2
It changes to (|00⟩+|01⟩)/√2, not the original state
It leaves the state exactly unchanged, since the state looks symmetric
questions.explain: Direct computation shows the reversed CNOT flips q1 on the |11⟩ term (since its control, q2, is 1), turning |11⟩ into |01⟩ and giving (|00⟩+|01⟩)/√2 — the 'looks symmetric so it must be invariant' intuition is wrong here.

questions.q: To build (|01⟩+|10⟩)/√2 starting from |10⟩, which gate sequence works?
options: Apply H to qubit 1, then CNOT with control=q1, target=q2
Apply H to qubit 2, then CNOT with control=q2, target=q1
Apply X to both qubits, then H to qubit 2
Apply CNOT first, then H to qubit 1
questions.explain: H on qubit 2 of |10⟩ gives (|10⟩+|11⟩)/√2; the reversed CNOT then flips q1 only on the |11⟩ term (control=q2=1), turning it into |01⟩, yielding (|01⟩+|10⟩)/√2 exactly.

questions.q: What does CZ do to the Bell state (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2?
options: Converts it to (|00⟩−|11⟩)/√2 by flipping the relative phase of the |11⟩ term
Leaves it completely unchanged
Converts it to (|01⟩+|10⟩)/√2
Collapses it to |00⟩
questions.explain: CZ multiplies only the |11⟩ amplitude by −1 (since CZ = diag(1,1,1,−1)), turning (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2 into (|00⟩−|11⟩)/√2 — a different Bell state with the same measurement probabilities.

questions.q: In Problem 1, why is it important to actually compute the matrix-vector product rather than reason from the state's symmetric appearance?
options: Because the 'symmetric-looking' intuition gives the wrong answer here — the reversed CNOT does change the state
Because matrix computation is always required even when two gates are provably identical
Because the state (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2 isn't actually a valid quantum state
Because CNOT only acts on basis states, never on superpositions
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly shows that assuming invariance from symmetry fails here — only the real computation reveals that the reversed CNOT transforms the state into (|00⟩+|01⟩)/√2.

questions.q: What is the key general lesson from Problems 2 and 3 about reaching a given Bell state?
options: The starting basis state never affects which gates are needed
There can be more than one valid gate sequence to reach the same Bell state, and extra gates like CZ can move between different Bell states via relative phase
CZ always destroys entanglement when applied to a Bell state
Only one gate sequence can ever produce any given Bell state
questions.explain: Problem 2 shows a different starting basis state needs a different (but equally valid) gate recipe, and Problem 3 shows CZ can convert one Bell state into another by changing a relative phase, without changing the measurement probabilities.
